subtopics.title: Factors, Not Terms — the Cancelling Law

questions.question: The cancelling law states that you may cancel:
options: Any matching symbols above and below the line
A FACTOR shared by the whole numerator and whole denominator — never a term
The largest term on each side
Anything, as long as you do it to both sides

questions.question: How can you CONVICT the illegal move of striking x² out of (x² − 25)/(x² + 8x + 15)?
options: By substituting a number: at x = 1 the original gives −1, the mutilated version does not
By checking that both x² terms have the same coefficient

questions.question: Factorised, (x² − 25)/(x² + 8x + 15) becomes:
A 'term' differs from a 'factor' because a term is:
options: Added or subtracted, while a factor multiplies the whole expression
Always the first item in an expression

subtopics.title: Multiplying, Dividing, and Denominators Hiding Cubes

questions.question: The FIRST move when dividing by an algebraic fraction is:
options: Invert the second fraction and multiply — before any cancelling

questions.question: (x² − 1)/(x + 4) ÷ (x + 1)/(x² − 16) simplifies to:
In (x³ + 8)/(x² − 4), the numerator factorises as:
After cancelling, (x² − 2x + 4)/(x − 2) must be left alone because:
options: The exam never requires further work
The top is irreducible and its parts are terms — nothing inside may cancel with the bottom

subtopics.title: Adding and Subtracting — the Lowest Common Denominator

questions.question: For 4/(x − 2) − 3/(x² − 4), the correct LCD is:
options: (x − 2)(x + 2) — each distinct factor once, not the product of the original denominators

questions.question: Rewritten over the LCD, the combined numerator of 4/(x − 2) − 3/(x² − 4) becomes:
The bracket in a subtracted numerator matters because:
options: It makes the working look neater
Brackets are required by convention only
The minus must distribute across EVERY term of the subtracted numerator — skipping the bracket flips only the first sign

questions.question: A fraction whose denominator equals zero is:
Restrictions must be read from:
options: The ORIGINAL denominators, before any cancelling

questions.question: For (x² − 25)/(x² + 8x + 15), which values of x are banned?
options: x ≠ −3 and x ≠ −5 — and the ban on −5 survives the cancellation

questions.question: Why does a DIVISION question restrict on the divisor's numerator too?
options: Because dividing by a fraction equal to zero is still dividing by zero
It does not — only denominators ever matter

subtopics.title: You Can Only Cancel a Whole Crate

questions.question: In the storeroom picture, the loose bottle on top of the crates represents:
options: A plus or minus sign that makes cancelling illegal

questions.question: Factorising, in the crates picture, is the job of:
options: Repacking a messy pile into sealed crates multiplied together

questions.question: The till-balancing check on (x² − 25)/(x² + 8x + 15) = (x − 5)/(x + 3) works by:
options: Substituting the same x into both and confirming the same value — at x = 1, both give −1
Checking the coefficients add to the same total

subtopics.title: Cut the Slices the Same Size Before You Add

questions.question: In the slicing picture, the denominator of a fraction is:
options: The slice size — and additions need both fractions cut to the same size

questions.question: Multiplying a fraction's top and bottom by (x + 2) to reach the LCD:
options: Is illegal unless x is known
Leaves its VALUE unchanged — only the slicing changes

questions.question: Subtracting the parcel (x − 4) from 3x + 2 gives 2x + 6 because:
options: The whole parcel is removed — subtract the x AND subtract the −4, which adds 4 back

questions.question: The final answer 2(x + 3)/(x − 5) shows one extra habit: after combining tops, you should:
options: Factorise the new numerator — it may reveal a final factor or simply a neater form

subtopics.title: The Numbers the Fraction Will Not Allow

questions.question: Sharing R360 among ZERO learners illustrates that:
options: Division by zero has NO answer — the question itself collapses

questions.question: After (x + 5) cancels out of a fraction, the ban on x = −5:
options: Stays in force — the original question issued it, and cancelling cannot lift it
Is lifted, since the factor is gone

questions.question: The four moves of the whole topic, in order, are:
options: Factorise; cancel whole factors only; match denominators with brackets on subtracted tops; state restrictions from the original bottoms
Add denominators, cancel terms, simplify, check
